topic: Vibe coding: Claude Design, Claude Code, GitHub, Vercel, Supabase

games.title: Untangle the Spaghetti
games.intro: Your Git flow got tangled in the colander. Put the five strands in the right order on the plates, from starting your own work to landing it in the main project. Tap a strand, or drag it onto a plate.
games.scoring: 100 if first check is correct, -20 per failed check, minimum 20

branch.label: Branch
branch.hint: Start your own strand of work, away from main

commit.label: Commit
commit.hint: Save a snapshot with a short note

push.label: Push
push.hint: Send your saved snapshots up to GitHub

pr.label: Pull request
pr.hint: Ask teammates to review your changes

merge.label: Merge
merge.hint: Combine the approved changes into main

games.recap: Branch → Commit → Push → Pull request → Merge. A commit saves locally and NOT on GitHub until you push. A push uploads straight away with no review; a pull request asks teammates to review first, and merging adds the approved changes to the main version.
games.fixHint: Tap the red plates to fix them.
games.poolEmptyMsg: Every strand is on a plate. Tap a plate to send one back.

games.title: Sauce Sorter
games.intro: Code snippets drop onto the counter. Throw each one in the right pot before the timer runs out: HTML is the pasta (the structure), CSS is the sauce (the style), JS is the spices (the action).

explain.html: HTML is the pasta: words and structure.
explain.css: CSS is the sauce: colours, fonts, spacing, phone vs laptop.
explain.js: JS is the spices: what happens on click, type, submit.

games.recap: **Remember the three files:** **index.html** holds the words and structure people read. **styles.css** holds the look: colours, fonts, spacing, phone vs laptop. **script.js** holds the behaviour: what happens on click, type or submit.
games.perfectText: Twelve out of twelve. The sauce is perfect

games.title: Dal Forno al Tavolo
games.intro: A dish goes from recipe to cooking to plating to serving. Match each LaunchLab tool to its station so the website gets from your idea to a live link on the table.
games.scoring: 100 if first check is correct, -20 per failed check, minimum 20

design.label: Claude Design
design.hint: Describe the look, no code needed

build.label: Claude Code
build.hint: Agentic coding that writes the real files

github.label: GitHub
github.hint: Store, share and collaborate on your repo

vercel.label: Vercel
vercel.hint: Builds and hosts at a public link

games.recap: Design → Build → GitHub → Vercel. Design the front end first in Claude Design, use "Handoff to Claude Code…" in the Share menu to build it, push the repo to GitHub, then import that repo in Vercel. From then on every push rebuilds the live site, and every pull request gets its own preview link.
games.fixHint: Tap the red stations to fix them.
games.poolEmptyMsg: Every tool is at a station. Tap a station to send one back.

games.title: Il Quiz del Cameriere

questions.question: You want your own copy of a classmate’s repo on your GitHub account, to change without touching the original. You…
questions.explanation: A fork is your own copy on your GitHub account. Clone is what brings a repo down onto your computer.

questions.question: You just made a commit. Where are your changes now?
questions.explanation: A commit is a local snapshot with a note. It reaches GitHub only when you push.

questions.question: Which one asks teammates to review your changes before they reach the main project?
questions.explanation: A push uploads straight away with no approval. A pull request opens a discussion and review first.

questions.question: Your repo is connected to Vercel. What happens when you push?
options: Nothing until you upload a zip
Vercel rebuilds and updates the live site automatically
You get an email to approve it
questions.explanation: Once connected, Vercel watches the repo. Every push triggers a rebuild in seconds, with no manual uploading.

questions.question: What does every pull request get on Vercel?
options: A merge button on the live site
questions.explanation: Each pull request gets a preview link, so the team can see the changes before merging.

questions.question: What is the difference between GitHub and Vercel?
options: GitHub hosts websites, Vercel stores code
GitHub stores your code; Vercel builds it and hosts it at a public link
questions.explanation: Nothing on GitHub is a website yet. Vercel reads the repo, builds the site and hosts it at a link that updates on every push.

questions.question: In Claude Design, where is the bridge that sends your design into Claude Code?
options: You have to copy the code by hand
questions.explanation: Open Share in the top right and find "Handoff to Claude Code…". Locate it before you start: it is easy to miss.

questions.question: A login token is best described as…
options: A temporary sticker saying "this is James" that expires on its own
A row in the user table
questions.explanation: Your browser shows the token on every request, so the site does not ask for your password on every click. Logging out throws it away.

questions.question: Which tool gives your site sign-up, log-in and a database of users?
questions.explanation: Supabase is an open-source backend-as-a-service for authentication, verification and a user database, and it connects to GitHub, Vercel and Lovable.

games.intro: The waiter has nine questions about Git, Vercel and logins. 10 points each.
games.perfectText: Nine for nine. The waiter is speechless

page.blurb: Vibe coding with Claude Design, Claude Code, GitHub and Vercel. Four mini-games to review the session: untangle Git, sort the sauce, serve the site and face the waiter's quiz.
